description: Every protected workflow and activation route the host-capability handshake gates. A route inside protected_surface_prefixes but absent from routes[] is blocked fail-closed until explicitly added; a route outside every prefix is reported not_protected so the gate cannot brick tool use it was never meant to police.
_independent_enforcement_note: MEASURED, not assumed: every route below reports independent_enforcement FALSE, because zero manifested entrypoints invoke the callsite named above. The field previously read true on all 12 routes while no entrypoint invoked the preflight -- a coverage claim with nothing behind it, and worse than an absent one, since this is the field a reader consults to ask whether a route is enforced anywhere the PreToolUse hook cannot be silently no-opped. FALSE here means UNSUPPORTED, not unprotected: the route is still blocked fail-closed by the gate and by evaluate_activation(), and independent_enforcement is a COVERAGE annotation that is recorded on the decision record, never a verdict input. Refusing on it once produced a refusal no state could satisfy. A route flips to true only when its entrypoint actually invokes the per-route preflight, which cannot be landed until a live PASS is reachable on a real host -- until then a blocking preflight would refuse every protected workflow. hooks/tests/test_capability_gate.py::test_independent_enforcement_claims_match_reality asserts the claim against reality in BOTH directions, so neither a stale true nor a stale false can survive.
_surface_note: The prefixes are intentionally the bare route-class tags, not 'slashcommand:/'. A malformed or empty slash-command route classifies as 'slashcommand:' and must land INSIDE the surface so it blocks fail-closed; a narrower prefix would let it fall outside and be treated as ordinary traffic.
_dispatch_route_note: tool:Agent and tool:Task were REMOVED from the surface (and the subagent-dispatch route deleted) because subagent dispatch has no non-hook entrypoint this harness controls. Keeping it in the surface bought ZERO protection on the threat host -- one that lists the gate and never dispatches it, where the gate never runs at all -- while inflicting a permanent, unsatisfiable block on a healthy host: the evaluator refused before ever loading state, so not even a fresh valid PASS could permit a dispatch. STATUS: OPEN COVERAGE REDUCTION -- direct subagent dispatch is UNGATED on every host. An earlier version of this note claimed dispatch stayed gated TRANSITIVELY through the workflows that perform it (/dev, /dev-command, /dev-overnight, /close, /commit). That claim is RETRACTED as measurably false: classify_route() maps a direct dispatch to tool:Agent / tool:Task, which never presents a SlashCommand envelope, so the manifested slash-command workflows cannot gate it. The workflows are gated; the route is not, and nothing gates a dispatch issued outside them. VERIFIED FACT (which stands): no non-hook enforcement point for this route exists in this harness, so refusing it refused it on grounds no state could satisfy. POLICY INFERENCE (stated separately, because clause (E) denies it): that this licenses removal from the surface rather than reporting the route unsupported. RESTORATION CONDITION -- both limbs, not either: (1) a reachable live PASS on a real host, and (2) an entrypoint consumer that invokes independent_enforcement_callsite for the route. Until both hold, restoring the routes only re-creates the unsatisfiable refusal. tool:Agent additionally serves as the NON-FLOOR NEGATIVE CONTROL for the repair floor in hooks/lib/capability_state.py: it must keep refusing in every degraded state, and admitting it to that floor would make this open reduction permanent in the degraded state as well.
_escape_hatch_note: Routes flagged human_consent_escape_hatch are PERMITTED even when handshake state is absent. Fail-closed must not mean fail-sealed: these are the harness's two documented human-authorisation routes, and blocking them on an unprotected host removes the only in-harness path by which a human could authorise a repair. Both carry `disable-model-invocation: true`, so neither is reachable from a model turn, and neither performs a privileged operation itself -- each records consent that OTHER gates consult, and those gates remain fully in force. The exemption is recorded on every decision record so it is auditable, never silent.

routes.why_protected: Orchestrates subagents that edit the tree; relies on hook-enforced tool policy and orchestrator gating.
Same pipeline as /dev, targeting harness command definitions.
Unattended multi-cycle loop and the sole branch/PR/worktree bypass; the highest-value route to gate.
Evidence-gated closeout; its verdict is trusted downstream.
Stages and commits repository state via an agentic subagent.
Publishes commits outside the machine; gated on a nonce-keyed push-analyst grant.
Mutates branch topology behind a nonce-keyed merge-analyst grant.
The only sanctioned SendMessage path; human-only and credential-minting.
Mints structured sentinel grants that relax the Bash safety boundary.
routes.why_exempt: Human-only break-glass (disable-model-invocation: true). It never overrides a settings DENY and only narrows one declared hook's refusal, so exempting it cannot widen the boundary beyond what a human explicitly typed -- while blocking it would strand a human on an unprotected host with no way to authorise the repair.

Human-only consent (disable-model-invocation: true). It relaxes the orchestrator gate only; the permanently-blocked tools, the Bash safety hook and the settings DENY list are all unaffected. Exempting it is what preserves a human repair path on a state-absent host.

routes.why_protected: Generates checkpoint state that later gates subagent exit.
Delegates work to an external CLI with repository access.
